format: The shared Markdown corpus. Core (markdown-parser.test.ts, Markdown.test.ts) and Rust (widget/markdown.rs, tests/markdown.rs) run this file. A row is [name, chunks, html, fails, text?].

name starts with the row's source: spec (CommonMark 0.31.2), gfm (GFM 0.29 extensions), parity (Core and Rust disagreements, records 540, 561, 567), fixture (whole documents), reflow and stream (chunked streams), math (extensions: ["math"]).
chunks are the appends of a stream; the document is their concatenation. A runner streams a row in its chunks, or a one-chunk row in 32 pieces of equal code point count.

html is what the specs say the whole document renders to, in canonical form: no whitespace next to a block tag (p, h1-h6, pre, ul, ol, li, blockquote, hr, table, thead, tbody, tr, th, td), no newline after
, no slash in void tags, and ' unescaped. GFM extensions are on. Math rows use and code blocks of the language math (tracks/markdown-extensions-1464.md).

fails lists the runners that disagree with the row, so the side the spec says is right is the row: marked (Core's parseMarkdownIncremental tokens through marked's HTML renderer), marked-stream (Core's streaming parse after each chunk against a fresh parse of the text so far), rust (Rust's block tree against html's block tags), rust-stream (the Rust widget's streamed blocks after each chunk against a fresh parse), core-text and rust-text (frames). A runner fails a row whose result does not match its listing, either way.

text, when present, holds the frame shown after each chunk, 60 columns wide with markup concealed, each line trimmed at its end; the last one is after streaming ends. Streams hold back what could still change kind (D93 Q4 B).

Rows named `spec N` are example N of the CommonMark Spec 0.31.2 by John MacFarlane (https://spec.commonmark.org/0.31.2/), released under CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/; LICENSE-COMMONMARK-SPEC). Rows named `gfm N` are example N of the GitHub Flavored Markdown Spec 0.29-gfm (https://github.github.com/gfm/), a derivative of the CommonMark Spec by GitHub, Inc., also under CC BY-SA 4.0. Their markdown is copied unchanged (the GFM spec's → is a tab); their HTML is adapted to the canonical form above, and examples 602, 606, 608, 611 and 612 take the GFM extended-autolink answer of cmark-gfm. This file is an adaptation shared under the same license.
